// diagnostic

E0404

`ok`/`err` need a fallible context

What

`ok`/`err` need a fallible context

Why

`ok` and `err` build a fallible result, so they only make sense where one is expected

Fix

Use `ok` or `err` only inside a fallible function or expression.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0404: tests/ui/fallible_unchecked.stderr.

Error [jet.OkErrOutsideFallible]: `Ok(...)` only fits where a fallible result is expected
  --> tests/ui/fallible_unchecked.jet:6:8
    |
  6 |     x: Ok(1)
    |        ^^^^
 Why: `Ok` builds the success side of a `T E!` result
 Fix: Use it in a `T E!` return type, a `T E!` binding annotation, or a call that expects one
